note: Written by hand after reading every error the shipped model made on the test sites (reports/errors.json: 5 false positives, 28 false negatives at the shipped threshold; fewer than the 50 + 50 planned because the test set has only 94 positives). Merged into the manifest by train/card.py.
failurePatterns: Images in a product or brand grid with a pointer cursor are flagged although nothing handles their clicks (all 5 false positives were product images on one shop page).
Game boards are missed: chess squares and similar grids of plain divs with no pointer cursor and no button-like class names scored just under the threshold (0.48 against 0.51).
Cards whose only content is an image, like the rock, paper and scissors choices, are missed: there is no text or class word to go on.

Some misses are not really controls: the crawler labels a container as clickable when it carries one listener for its children (an FAQ wrapper, a list, a <main>). These are label noise of the delegation kind, at container level.
A div with an inline onclick but no pointer cursor and no button-like class ("Search User") was missed: the model leans on the cursor and on class words.
limitations: It was trained on a stand-in corpus of hobby and teaching projects from GitHub, not on the planned Tranco crawl of popular sites. Treat it as a demonstration until it is retrained on the Tranco crawl.
React, Vue and Angular pages are almost absent from the training data (a handful of pages), so it has not been measured on framework-built sites.
The test websites hold 94 click-only controls, most of them on a few sites, so every percentage on this page has a wide margin; the 95% intervals are shown where they were measured.
The model in use is the gradient-boosting baseline: the graph network missed the ship gate. Its scores still come from the same 552 cues and the same calibration.
labelProbeReading: Read by hand: the 12 disagreements on pages used for training are 5 hover-effect squares (moving the mouse to click recolours them), 4 countdown timers that tick every second, 1 list item whose content is a button, and 2 unclear (a 'Blog' paragraph and an icon image). None is clearly a click-only control the labeller missed, so the probe's rate is a loose upper bound.
